Changelog

boundarylogic 0.2.0 (2026-11-07)

Changes since 0.1.0. The measured effect of each change to the method, on the loan harness and on the Pima example of Paper 1, is in documentation/methodology-changes/methodology-changes.md.

Breaking changes

Data and models

  • bl_prepare_data() removes outliers itself, through the new argument hull_fraction (default 1: no rows removed, since the thesis makes outlier removal optional), and returns a "bl_filter_result". The two-step bl_prepare_data() |> bl_filter_outliers() is one call. Pass hull_fraction = 0.9 to remove the outermost 10% of the training rows, as the thesis’s loan example, the loan harness and the vignette do. bl_filter_outliers() keeps its default of 0.9 (calling it means filtering is wanted) and stays exported for use after bl_wrap_data().
  • bl_fit_model() fits four model types, all through parsnip: GLM, SVM, NNET and RForest (a decision tree, rpart). It no longer fits GAM, GBM, LDA or XGB: fit these yourself and pass them to bl_wrap_model() (see its predict_fn contract for custom and GAM models; an XGB model is passed as list(model = <xgboost model>, features = <character vector>)).
  • The model type RForrest is renamed RForest in bl_fit_model(), bl_wrap_model(), .fit_model() and .pred_function(). The old spelling still works at all four, with a warning.
  • bl_build_grid() and bl_build_result() replace rounding with b_margin, the half-width of the decision-boundary contour band, set directly (default 0.001, which rounding = 3L gave). bl_find_local_cf() reads it from bl_result$b_margin. Model predictions are unaffected: they are always floor-rounded to 3 decimals.

Plots

  • plot_biplotEZ() loses boundary, show_arrows and arrow_col. Counterfactual arrows are drawn by bl_pick_point(bl_result, bl_boundary = ...), one per click: drawing every arrow at plot time raised zero-length-arrow warnings that could not be suppressed.
  • no_points is renamed plot_points in plot_biplotEZ() and plot.bl_local_result(), with the positive meaning (TRUE shows the points). The defaults keep each plot’s look. (plot.bl_surrogate() has neither argument; it always draws its points.)
  • plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_sparse_result() stop with an error when given rotate_deg (0.1.0 ignored it). The local biplot’s orientation comes from the optimal rotation (.bl_rotate()), which is part of the method, and is never turned further. rotate_deg is for viewing the global biplot: plot_biplotEZ() and plot.bl_surrogate().
  • In plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_surrogate() the axis labels default to label_dir = "Paral" (the direction adapts to the border; it was "Hor"), and label_offset_dist defaults to 1.5 (it was 0.5).

Search results

  • bl_find_local_cf() applies the thesis’s plausibility rule (section 4.3.1): for each component pair it builds the convex hull of the training data on the rotated plane, and keeps only the boundary points inside it, before the actionability constraints, the training ranges and the model re-score. The global biplot’s hull is not used, since the rotation invalidates its coordinates. The hull is built from the training data alone (Appendix A of the thesis also includes the target), so a target outside the training data gets a counterfactual inside it. The result gains hull and hull_polygon (the winning plane’s hull, stored also with the hull switched off, for the plot), and the no-solution message names the hull. On the loan harness the new applicant’s counterfactual has a credit score of 534.92; without the hull it would be 489.44. See documentation/local-convex-hull.md.
  • set_filters() holds all three of the thesis’s constraints on a counterfactual (section 4.3.1, p.116): actionability (the per-variable constraints), plausibility (hull = TRUE, above) and feasibility (train_ranges = TRUE, every feature within its training range). Both switches are on by default, and set_filters = NULL in bl_find_local_cf() keeps them on. set_filters(tgt, hull = FALSE, train_ranges = FALSE) with no per-variable constraint gives the unconstrained counterfactual (thesis p.115). With train_ranges = FALSE the restored "fixed" and rounded "integer" points are not checked against the ranges either. The result gains the logical field train_ranges; a search with a rule switched off prints Not applied, and print(<bl_filters>) shows both switches. A feature named hull or train_ranges cannot be constrained through set_filters().
  • The empty-region rule (thesis section 3.10, step 4: a boundary area that contains no data is discarded) is judged on the training data, in both searches, through the private helper .encloses_data(). In bl_find_boundary() a contour that is still closed after the hull clip is kept only if it encloses training rows; in 0.1.0 the rows being searched decided, so a row’s counterfactual could depend on the other rows passed in data or tdp. bl_find_local_cf() applies the same rule on each rotated plane when the hull is on. On the loan harness the global search keeps 18 contours (with the searched rows deciding it would keep 12, and 346 of the 4,429 test counterfactuals would differ), and without the rule the constrained counterfactual of test row 13 would lie on a closed contour with no training data inside.
  • The distance follows the thesis rule by projection (thesis section 3.9.1): Euclidean for a PCA biplot, Mahalanobis for a CVA biplot. The new argument distance = c("auto", "mahalanobis", "euclidean"), whose default "auto" the private .resolve_distance() turns into that rule, sets it in bl_find_local_cf() (the comparison of component pairs and the "integer" rounding) and in plot.bl_boundary() / bl_robustness() (the per-variable standardisation). In 0.1.0 the local search compared the pairs by the distance on the rotated plane, and the importance divided each variable by its total standard deviation (X_sd).
    • Under CVA the pair choice is unchanged: the CVA loadings satisfy V'WV = I/(n-g), so the squared Mahalanobis distance is n - g times the squared plane distance for every pair. The importance divides by the within-class standard deviation, sqrt(diag(W)), which raises features that separate the classes well; pass distance = "euclidean" for the 0.1.0 importance.
    • Under PCA the pairs are compared by the Euclidean distance in X-space, each feature divided by its total standard deviation. For a standardised PCA this equals the plane distance at the search’s point (the rotated loadings are orthonormal), and it also measures the "integer" candidates, which lie off the plane. The importance is as in 0.1.0.
  • bl_find_local_cf()’s max_pairs default is 21L (was 10L), so the search tries every component pair for up to 7 features, as the thesis does. Results change for models with 6 or more features: more pairs are tried, the selected pair can change, and run time grows with the number of pairs. Pass max_pairs = 10L for the 0.1.0 search.
  • A "fixed" constraint holds exactly. The search still accepts a fixed feature within 0.5 model units, because a point on the 2D boundary rarely holds a feature at exactly its observed value (0.1.0 reported that point). bl_find_local_cf() then sets each fixed feature the search moved back to its observed value. When the restored point still crosses the boundary and lies within train_ranges, it is the counterfactual. Otherwise there is none: solution_found is FALSE, and blocking_constraint (also given as a message) says where the search moved the fixed feature, why the restored point fails, and that changing the constraints on the actionable features may make a counterfactual possible. The new field fixed_check records the outcome and the search’s own point. See documentation/fixed-constraint-restore.md.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf() selects features greedily: it changes the "Supports" features one at a time, largest Shapley value first, re-scores the model after each, and stops once the boundary is crossed. Features not needed stay at their observed values. The new field sparse_path records each step, and print() shows it. In 0.1.0 every "Supports" feature was changed. See documentation/sparse-counterfactual.md.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf()’s round_to is deprecated: a non-NULL value stops with a message. It rounded in model units (z-scores for a standardised model), one value for every feature, without re-checking the constraints, and could reverse a move and invalidate the sparse counterfactual. On the loan harness (target 13, credit_score = "increase"), round_to = 1 moved loan_percent_income up from 0.05 to 0.0666 instead of down to 0.0484, and the sparse path never crossed the boundary (0.483, against 0.547 without rounding). Mark a whole-number feature "integer" in set_filters() instead (see New features). round_to = NULL still runs.
  • bl_shapley() adds a "No effect" class for a Shapley value of 0 (up to 1e-8): the feature’s change never moves the prediction. In 0.1.0 such a feature was "Supports" for a class-0 target, and so was changed in the sparse counterfactual, and "Contradicts" for a class-1 target.
  • bl_shapley()’s seed default is NULL (was 1L): it seeds the random number generator only when asked, so repeated calls on the permutation path (more than exact_max_vars features) are no longer silently identical. The exact path (the default for up to 14 features) is deterministic and ignores seed.

New features

  • Raw units. bl_set_scaling() records the transform standardised = (raw - center) / scale applied to the features before the model was fitted, on a bl_data or bl_filter_result; it flows into bl_result$scaling. It is display-only: the projection, the grid and what the model sees do not change. With it, the biplot plot methods (plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_projection(), plot.bl_local_result(), plot.bl_sparse_result(), plot.bl_surrogate()) label their axes in raw units, print.bl_result() says so, and the prints and plots that show feature values (targets, counterfactuals, Shapley values, the sparse counterfactual) show them in raw units. bl_apply_scaling(data, bl_result) converts new raw-unit data, such as an external applicant, to the model’s units, which every function that takes new data expects (bl_select_target(), bl_project_points(), plot(..., target_point =)). bl_select_target() warns when a data-frame target lies outside the training ranges, and suggests bl_apply_scaling() when converting would bring it inside.
  • bl_find_local_cf() returns the counterfactual as a "bl_counterfactual" object (field bl_counterfactual), parallel to bl_target: the boundary point’s values in model units, its prediction and class, and the scaling. print.bl_counterfactual() shows the values in raw units when a scaling is set. print.bl_target() and print.bl_counterfactual() take a digits argument, which print.bl_local_result() uses to keep its blocks consistent.
  • Every biplot plot method takes new_title for a custom title: plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_surrogate() gain it, and plot.bl_result() and plot.bl_sparse_result() pass it on through ... (plot_biplotEZ() had it). plot.bl_projection() does not take it.
  • Mahalanobis distance. bl_build_projection() computes the within-class metric W, its inverse (by Cholesky, with a ridge fallback) and its type (metric, metric_inv, metric_type), which flow through bl_assemble() into bl_result. Under CVA it is the W of the CVA eigenproblem, so distances measured with it agree with the biplot axes.
    • bl_find_local_cf() returns dist_mahalanobis, all_distances_mahalanobis, dist_x, all_distances_x and distance, and its print shows them.
    • bl_find_boundary() returns dist_mahalanobis, the squared Mahalanobis distance of each observation’s move to its boundary point, v' W^-1 v with v = B_x - x_obs: the same quantity as the local search’s, so global and local distances can be compared. print() shows the mean of its square root.
    • plot.bl_boundary() prints a Mahalanobis check, which compares the squared length of the plotted per-feature distances, sum(vec_to_boundary_sd^2), with the full v' W^-1 v, notes when the difference is at least 25% of the full distance, and returns the numbers as mahalanobis_check.
    • A bl_result without metric_inv (built by 0.1.0) falls back to Euclidean with a warning (dist_mahalanobis is then NA). See documentation/boundary-distance-and-robustness.md.
  • set_filters() accepts an "integer" constraint for a whole-number feature (a count or a score): "integer" alone, with a direction, c("increase", "integer"), or with a range, list(c(min, max), "integer"). Without it a feature is continuous. bl_find_local_cf() searches as before, then rounds the counterfactual: for each integer feature it tries the whole values just below and above, in raw units when a scaling is set, keeps the combinations that still cross the boundary and meet every constraint and train_ranges, and takes the nearest by the search’s selector. When none is valid it reports no counterfactual, with the reason. The Shapley values and the sparse counterfactual use the rounded point. The new field integer_check records the outcome, and print() explains it.
  • plot.bl_local_result() (and plot.bl_sparse_result() through it) colours the prediction grid only inside the plane’s convex hull of the training data, as the global biplot colours only inside its hull: the coloured area is where the search could choose boundary points. The new argument trim_to_hull (NULL, the default, follows the search; TRUE also shows the hull of a search with the hull switched off; FALSE colours the whole grid). Display only. The plot also widens its window when the target or the counterfactual lies outside the training points, so a new applicant beyond the training data is drawn.
  • plot() works on a bl_result (new plot.bl_result(), which calls plot_biplotEZ()), as on a bl_local_result, bl_sparse_result and bl_surrogate.
  • plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_surrogate() gain ticks_var/ticks_n for per-variable tick counts (the pattern of label_offset_var/label_offset_dist), and label_offset_var accepts variable names as well as indices. plot.bl_local_result() gains label_cex, and plot.bl_surrogate() gains rotate_deg.
  • print() of a bl_local_result ends with an observed / counterfactual / change / constraint table, plus a note on any "fixed" feature the search moved and any "integer" feature it rounded. print() of a bl_shapley uses the same layout with shapley and contribute columns and the Shapley sum, and print() of a bl_sparse_result with sparse and used columns and the sparse path. The tables, the Target and Counterfactual blocks and the sparse path print in fixed notation with 2 decimals, in raw units when a scaling is set; a feature whose change would print as 0.00 gets more decimals (up to 4) in its row. The display rules are written up in documentation/scaling_axis_relabel_note.md.
  • plot.bl_shapley() labels every variable "variable: observed -> counterfactual", with the decimals of the tables, and shows the Shapley value on each bar, unclipped. The x-axis reads “Impact on prediction (Shapley value)”.
  • The "XGB" model type accepts models from xgboost::xgboost() (class "xgboost"), which are scored from the data frame because their predict method refuses an xgb.DMatrix. bl_wrap_model() stops unless such a model is a binary:logistic classifier on levels "0"/"1": fitted with a numeric response, xgboost() gives a regression. xgb.train() boosters are scored as in 0.1.0.
  • bl_pick_point() gains bl_boundary: given a bl_find_boundary() result, it draws the arrow from each clicked point to its boundary point.
  • bl_surrogate() reports hull_coverage, n_in_hull and n_total, which print.bl_surrogate() shows beside the accuracy.
  • bl_build_projection() checks the condition number of V (kappa(V, exact = FALSE)) before inverting it, returns it as condition_number, and warns above 1e10.
  • bl_find_boundary() says how many of its counterfactuals lie outside the training feature ranges; they are retained.
  • bl_find_local_cf() warns when the target lies at the centre of the biplot: the Procrustes cross-product is then zero, the rotation is undefined, and every component pair gives the plane of components (1,2).

Bug fixes and other improvements

  • .bl_rotate(): when the selected component pair is not (1, 2), the target no longer collapses to the biplot origin. Vrho/tVrho are sliced to columns/rows (1, 2), which the SVD construction guarantees.
  • bl_find_boundary(), bl_surrogate() and bl_find_local_cf() are deterministic. Their shared helper .nearest_idx_block() picked the nearest contour vertex with max.col(-d2), whose default ties.method = "random" treats every vertex within 1e-5 of the farthest vertex’s squared distance as tied and draws one from the session’s random-number stream, so results could change between repeated calls. It now takes the exact nearest vertex (ties.method = "first"). The behaviour was inherited from the PhD code. In the loan harness, 1-3% of global counterfactuals could change under the old rule; taking the exact vertex moved the v1 robustness total from 9203.63 to 9203.29 and the surrogate accuracies from 0.8334/0.8843 to 0.8337/0.8845. The old rule also caused the repeat-call differences in the rotation scripts (17_1, 17_3) that had been put down to the plane’s under-determination. See documentation/nearest-vertex-tie-break.md.
  • bl_build_grid() takes its cutoff from the model (cutoff = bl_model$cutoff) and stores it as bl_grid$cutoff; bl_assemble() stops if the grid’s and the model’s cutoffs differ. In 0.1.0 the grid always drew its contours at 0.5, while the searches used bl_result$cutoff, so a model with another cutoff gave a global boundary at one threshold and a local one at another. Results at the default 0.5 are unchanged.
  • bl_build_grid() clamps the grid’s predictions to [0, 1], with a warning that reports how many cells were clamped, and bl_find_local_cf() clamps its grid scores the same way, with one warning per call. A custom predict_fn returning values outside [0, 1] gave missing colours, silently dropped cells, or stopped the search with an error.
  • plot_biplotEZ(grid_col =) splits the two-colour grid at the model’s cutoff, not at a fixed 0.5. bl_build_grid() no longer computes the unused inside_data.
  • Every biplot uses the thesis colours for the four prediction outcomes: TP red, TN blue, FP purple, FN orange. plot.bl_projection() (through bl_build_projection()’s point_col) used green, steel blue, orange and red, so red meant FN there and TP everywhere else. The colours are held in one private constant, .confusion_cols (R/utils.R).
  • bl_build_projection() with CVA: if a TP/TN/FP/FN group is empty, a message names it and the empty level is dropped, as is any empty level of a user-supplied cva_classes, so CVA and the metric W count only groups with rows. plot.bl_projection() uses the confusion colours for any subset of the four groups; with an empty group it coloured every point blue.
  • plot.bl_local_result() colours the target by its own true class. It looked the class up in test_data by row number, which gave another observation’s class whenever bl_select_target() indexed a different data frame. bl_target gains a class_obs field; a one-row data frame target that includes the class column gets its confusion colour too.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf(): used_in_sparse is FALSE for a "fixed" feature, which the sparse counterfactual always reverts. It followed the Shapley classification alone and could read TRUE for a feature the sparse counterfactual did not change.
  • label_offset_dist and ticks_n stay paired with their own variables when label_offset_var or ticks_var names a variable the model does not have, and a warning flags a value vector whose length is neither 1 nor the length of its variable vector. Affects plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_surrogate() (display only).
  • bl_prepare_data(), bl_filter_outliers(), bl_build_grid() and bl_build_result() no longer change the active graphics device when more than one device is open. The internal helpers .build_hull_polygon() and .bl_get_plot_bounds() restore the caller’s device after closing their temporary png().
  • bl_find_local_cf()’s per-pair search applies the actionability constraints before train_ranges, so a segment that fails the more selective rule is dropped early.
  • .poly_clip(), the internal hull filter, is defined once, in R/hull_utils.R. The copy in R/boundary.R was never used (the other replaced it at load time) and is removed. Results are unchanged.
  • print.bl_result() and summary.bl_result() label the stored hull fraction as the grid hull (outlie, default 1), not as the outlier filter’s fraction, which bl_prepare_data() applies earlier.
  • bl_assemble() no longer fails with bl_model = NULL; bl_build_result() stops with an error where it returned invisible(NULL); print.bl_points() prints "(no model)" when there are no model predictions; .fit_model() warns on unknown hyperparameters passed in model_params.
  • DESCRIPTION lists grDevices, graphics, stats and utils under Imports, matching the NAMESPACE imports.
  • The help pages and messages of bl_find_local_cf() and plot.bl_local_result() say “component pair”, not “eigenvector pair”: each pair labels a plane through the target, which the Procrustes rotation turns, so the selected plane need not coincide with the plane of the two components that name it.
  • The help of plot.bl_boundary() and bl_robustness() says that the variable importance and robustness measure the in-plane gap to the boundary, as the thesis does, while bl_find_boundary()’s dist_x and dist_mahalanobis also include the observation’s part off the biplot plane and are reported only.
  • The loan-default vignette is rewritten for package users. It follows the development harness on the full data: the same models, the five pruned variables, the refit on standardised features with bl_set_scaling(), test row 13 with the harness’s constraints, and the new applicant converted with bl_apply_scaling(). Each step gives the code, a table of the parameters that matter and how to read the output, and it ends with the SHAP comparison. It does not call bl_robustness(): the pruning reads the totals plot() returns. The vignette is precomputed: vignettes/precompile.R knits Boundary_Logic_loan_default_workflow.Rmd.orig into the shipped .Rmd and its figures, so building the package runs no vignette code.
  • The README’s constraint example finds a counterfactual and shows its output.
  • The technical notes in documentation/ describe the method and the code: the boundary distance and robustness, the biplot rotation and the choice of plane, the fixed-feature restore, the sparse counterfactual, the local convex hull, the raw-unit display, the nearest-vertex tie-break, and the stepwise algorithms (documentation/algorithms.md).
  • Documentation brought in line with the code across the roxygen help, the README, the vignette prose, the implementation summary and the code walkthroughs (for example: bl_build_result(bl_model = NULL) returns a model-free bl_result; bl_filter_outliers() takes a bl_data from bl_wrap_data(); dist_z / dist_mahalanobis belong to the winning pair only; bl_predict() rounds to 3 decimals; the @return fields of bl_surrogate() and bl_build_projection() match the objects).

boundarylogic 0.1.0 (2026-03-25)

  • Initial implementation of the full three-phase Boundary Logic workflow:
    • Phase 1 — data preparation (bl_prepare_data(), bl_wrap_data(), bl_filter_outliers()), model fitting/wrapping (bl_fit_model(), bl_wrap_model()), PCA/CVA biplot projection (bl_build_projection()), prediction-grid and decision-boundary contour construction (bl_build_grid()), and assembly into the central bl_result anchor object (bl_assemble(), bl_build_result()), with plot_biplotEZ() for visualisation.
    • Phase 2 (global) — nearest-boundary counterfactual search (bl_find_boundary()), distance-to-boundary plots and per-variable robustness summaries (plot.bl_boundary(), bl_robustness()), and a spatial surrogate model (bl_surrogate()).
    • Phase 3 (local) — single-observation target selection (bl_select_target()), actionability constraints (set_filters()), local counterfactual search via biplot rotation (bl_find_local_cf()), Shapley attribution of the counterfactual path (bl_shapley()), and sparse counterfactual generation (bl_find_sparse_cf()).
  • Interactive biplot point picker bl_pick_point().
  • bl_predict() and bl_project_points() for scoring and projecting arbitrary data frames into the biplot’s Z-space.
  • Bundled the Pima Indians Diabetes and loan-default datasets, with accompanying vignettes covering the complete workflow end to end.
